findings.summary: My change-request text is silently swallowed. I typed a 113-character reaction ('Approach 1 wins. One thing: the tip % buttons feel cramped — make them big thumb-sized pills, at least 48px tall.') into the Studio prompt and sent it; a new version v5 ('3 file(s) from prompt') was generated, but my exact words are never shown anywhere again — the conversation lane keeps showing only the original brief prompt, version rows show a bare 'prompt' chip with no text, and the Tweaks tab is a design-token editor. There is no way to verify what I entered came back intact; the input field comes back empty and the text is unrecoverable.

An approved design cannot be handed to the builders: 'Promote to build' opens a dialog showing a prior attempt 'Deferred, resumes ~06:38', and clicking 'Confirm and compile' fails with 'Refusing to promote a preview that reported an error: the governor is holding sessions back (reserve) — no planner ran'. Tasks list shows (0), so my approved v5 never reached the Board while background autopilot kept consuming the same session budget (29/40 → 32/40 · 0 free during my session).

The design session got stuck in a 'drafting' state I never requested (after v5 completed and returned to 'approved'), with Approve and Promote disabled for over 8 minutes; the Stop button did nothing. Only a full page reload recovered the session to its true 'approved' state.

At the default viewport, the Critique panel overlaps the Versions/Tweaks rail and intercepts all pointer events — clicks on 'v5' and 'Tweaks' time out repeatedly ('subtree intercepts pointer events'). The same elements become clickable only after enlarging the viewport to 1920×1400, and the bug returns in every new tab.

What the product did store, it kept: version v5 created from my prompt, the 'approved' status, and all eight design files (approach 1–3 calculator + settings, merged calculator.html/settings.html) survived unchanged through /reload and through a brand-new tab navigating in fresh. The prototype batch stayed at the two screens I asked for — no scope padding.
